news.title: World Cup winner Llorente retires from Spain duty at 31
news.lede: Soccer Football - UEFA Champions League - Quarter Final - Second Leg - Atletico Madrid v FC Barcelona - Riyadh Air Metropolitano, Madrid, Spain - April 14, 2026 Atletico Madrid's Marcos Llorente reacts REUTERS/Gonzalo Fuentes. Sept 3 - World Cup winner Marcos Llorente announced his retirement from international football on Thursday, ending a Spain career that yielded 27 caps. The Atletico Madrid defender, 31, made his senior team debut for Spain in 2020 and was part of the squad that beat Argentina 1-0 to win the World Cup in July, although he remained on the bench in the final. "I realise that I’m still young and that, perhaps, if I continued to perform well, I’d still have years left to play in this jersey," Llorente wrote on Instagram.

news.title: 'It's been an honor' – World Cup winner Marcos Llorente retires from international football with Spain aged 31
news.lede: Atletico Madrid star Marcos Llorente has shocked the footballing world by announcing his immediate retirement from international football. Despite being just 31 years old and coming off the back of a historic World Cup victory, the versatile midfielder has decided to hang up his boots for La Roja. In a move that has caught many supporters by surprise, Llorente has confirmed his permanent retirement from the Spanish national team. The Atletico Madrid standout, who recently helped steer Spain to glory at the 2026 World Cup held across the United States, Canada, and Mexico, believes now is the right moment to step away from the international stage.

news.title: 2026 World Cup winner announces shock retirement from international football with Spain
news.lede: A shocking retirement announcement has rocked the football world, with Spanish star Marcos Llorente announcing his retirement from international football, leaving La Roja fans in disbelief. The 31-year-old announced on social media on Thursday that he is retiring from international football, just six years after making his debut for the national side. Llorente confirmed in a lengthy Instagram post that, after much consideration, he has decided to part ways with the Spanish national team. The Atletico Madrid star stressed that the decision was completely personal and had nothing to do with his playing time at the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

news.title: World Cup wishlists, early movers, big clearouts: 2026 summer transfer window trends
news.lede: At the end of a busy transfer window which spanned the World Cup, here are some of the subplots of the summer. The World Cup is always a good shop window. Yan Diomande was already a rising star at RB Leipzig but shining for Côte d’Ivoire in the US helped push up his price tag before a £115.7m move to Real Madrid. There were other breakout stars: Switzerland’s Johan Manzambi, whose signature Aston Villa pipped Newcastle to; Bosnia and Herzegovina’s Kerim Alajbegovic, who went to Juventus; and Ghana’s Caleb Yirenkyi, who is now in the Premier League with Coventry.
